reason: Start with the filter to follow what leaves the blood before the recovery stage.
expectation: I expect small substances, including useful ones and waste, to pass through while blood cells and large proteins stay behind.

alternatives.reason: Connecting the ureters would build the urine route, but I want to see filtering first.

effect: The filter lets useful glucose, salts and water through along with waste, so the recovery tube is the next step to follow.
reaction: It was interesting that the filter doesn't just select waste.
reason: Use the recovery tube to see what goes back into the blood.
expectation: I expect glucose, some salts and much of the water to return to the blood, leaving fluid containing waste.

alternatives.reason: The ureters would build the drainage route, but I want to follow the filtered fluid first.

effect: Recovery returns useful substances and much water to the blood, leaving a smaller volume containing waste. Next I can build the drainage route.
reaction: It makes sense why filtering alone isn't enough.
reason: Attach the ureters to start the route from the kidneys toward the bladder.
expectation: I expect the two ureters to connect to the kidney outlets, with their other ends leading toward the bladder.

alternatives.reason: The bladder also needs connecting, but the ureters are the route from the kidneys to it.

effect: The ureters are fitted, so the bladder is the next part of the drainage route.
reaction: The fitting was straightforward, though the picture description didn't show much new.
reason: Attach the bladder; it's the only offered combination and completes the route toward the storage sac.
expectation: I expect the ureters to connect the kidneys to the bladder.

effect: The bladder is fitted, and urine can travel through the ureters to collect there. I can now follow the recovered fluid through the route.
reaction: The explanation made the purpose of the tubes clear.
reason: Follow the kidney fluid to finish the filtering and recovery route.
expectation: I expect the remaining waste-containing fluid to become urine and travel toward the bladder.

alternatives.reason: Connecting the organs to the body also matters, but I want to follow the fluid first.

effect: The remaining fluid followed the kidney route into the bladder as urine, completing the filtering and recovery goal.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the route completed while blood stayed separate.
reason: Connect the urinary organs to the body; this is the only offered combination and addresses the remaining goal.
expectation: I expect the kidneys, ureters and bladder to be added to the body, with the kidneys connected to its blood supply.

effect: The kidneys, ureters and bladder are now connected to the body, completing the remaining goal.
reaction: The final picture made both the blood supply and urine's route out clear.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following the filtered fluid through recovery was most worthwhile: it showed why useful substances need to return to the blood rather than simply being discarded.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the ureters was less interesting because the result's picture description didn't show much new.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the filter lets useful glucose and water through along with waste.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, although fitting the bladder was the only offered combination at that point.

continue.text: Yes, I would choose to continue: following the fluid from filtering to the bladder made me curious about how another body system works.
